newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - March 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - March 10.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
GOVERNMENT UNDERTAKES DAMAGE CONTROL EXERCISE

The ruling United Front was engaged in a massive damage-control exercise in view of the public row between Home Minister Indrajit Gupta and Uttar Pradesh governor Romesh Bhandari. The prime minister was understood to be weighing the entire issue in the light of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) censure motion in the lower house demanding Bhandari's recall. Meanwhile, the Bahujan Samaj Party announced it would side with the BJP on the motion.
The Pioneer
LEFT PARTY MAY MOVE CUT MOTION AGAINST BUDGET

The Marxist Communist Party (CPM) wil press for the withdrawal of certain budgetary provisions like tax concessions, disinvestment commitment and opening up of the insurance sector. The CPM, a constituent of the ruling coalition, may also move cut motions in parliament against the budget. This was stated by the party's general secretary in a television interview and also endorsed by a politburo member at a press conference.
The Economic Times
RID INSURANCE SECTOR OF GILTS

Insurance companies should not be asked to invest 75 percent of investments in gilts, the finance secretary said. In his submission, he also stressed the need for changes in the sector. Highlighting his point, he said nowhere was the insurance sector asked to lock 75 percent of the company's assets in government securities.
AMEMDMENTS TO STRENGTHEN PATENT RULES SOON

After failing to introduce new legislation for patents registration, the government planned to make some amendments to the existing norms. The expert panel set up for the purpose was expected to finalise the new amendments soon. The major changes proposed by the panel include having a new structure for patents application and reducing the total number of forms to be filed for a patent.
Financial Express
L&T MAY EXPORT CEMENT TO SRI LANKA, BANGLADESH

Larsen & Toubro (L&T) has identified Sri Lanka and Bangladesh as potential markets for cement. The company now plans to set up clinker grinding units in these countries with capacities of 500,000 tonnes to 700,000 tonnes. The clinker would be supplied by L&T's cement plants in Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh. This would then be converted into cement and sold in the two countries.
ROADSHOWS FOR VSNL ISSUE BEGIN TODAY

The roadshows for Videsh Sanchar Nigam's (VSNL) Euroissue will begin on Monday. The offering is for 18.9 million shares in the form of 37.8 million global depositary receipts, each representing one half of an equity share. Pricing for the international offering is expected on March 24.
EXPORT CREDIT GUARANTEE CORP'S CAPITAL TO BE HIKED

The Commerce Ministry decided to expand the capital base of the Export Credit Guarantee Corporation (ECGC), the country's sole export insurance institution, from 750 million rupees to five billion. The capital infusion would be done in phases over the next four years. ECGC was on a restructuring exercise with Coopers & Lybrand preparing the recast plan.
Business Standard
NEW CAPITAL GAINS TAX RULE TRIGGERS SELLOFF IN BONDS

The stock market-friendly budget would hit the market for debentures and bonds issued by financial institutions and government firms. Some corporates were disposing of their holdings of bonds and debentures before the new budget came into effect on April 1, 1997. The flight from long-term debt was triggered off by a provision in the finance bill which withdrew the benefit of indexation in computing long-term capital gains tax on such instruments.
INFLATION RATE DROPS TO 7.9 PCT

The annual rate of inflation declined marginally to 7.91 percent during the week ended February 28 after remaining static at 7.99 percent during the two previous weeks. This was the 100th week in succession that inflation maintained single digit levels. It fell into the single-digit range in April 1995.
$300 MLN FORD PLAN FOR TWO WHOLLY OWNED SUBSIDIARIES

Ford Motor Co will invest about $300 million in setting up two fully-owned subsidiaries in the country. In two applications, Ford sought approval to set up an automated components division (ACD) and electrical and fuel handling division (EFHD) companies. The first venture, to be called AC India, was cleared while the proposal for the EFHD project would be taken up later.
The Observer
MARKET SET TO SOBER UP FURTHER

The Bombay stock market (BSE) may temporarily be out of the budget euphoria as prices were set to decline in the coming week. Market conditions indicated an overbought position as outstanding business of 1.41 billion rupees was reported at the end of the settlement ended March 6, as against 950 million in the previous settlement, a BSE member said. Analysts were of the view that a mild reaction of around 150 points in the BSE index could set to allow the market to adjust.
Business Line
PRICE STAMPING ON YARN TO BE REINTRODUCED

The Textiles Ministry decided to reintroduce the compulsory price stamping on yarn. It decided to amend the norms to take care of the interests of both yarn manufacturers and consumers. The revamped norms would bring both yarn and fabric under the compulsory price stamping.
